title: What the dead fear
summary: Why the afterlife is no second chance.

claims.text: Many of the Restless take their state as a second chance with a kind of immortality, and soon learn otherwise: their existence can still end.
The Shadow pushes each wraith toward selfish and cruel acts, Spectres hunt the living dead, and even in Stygia the Hierarchy may judge a wraith useless and send it to the forges.

title: The Shroud in disasters
summary: How catastrophe thins the wall between living and dead.

claims.text: A disaster big enough to send warnings ahead of it thins the local Shroud, which is why the dead so often warn relatives in ghost stories; the Shroud thins further as death and fear spread, and stays thin until the next dawn.
Ordinary catastrophe cannot thin the Shroud past a set limit; only a supernatural disaster that breaks the barriers between worlds can fuse the Skinlands and Shadowlands completely.

title: The Vasa diving bell
summary: A relic for exploring the drowned Tempest.

claims.text: A black studded bell, big enough for one wraith, turned up in the Tempest after the Viking-era warship Vasa was found in Stockholm harbor; it hides its user from searching eyes underwater.
St. Elmo's fire lanterns, rarely seen outside the Underworld, light routes through the Tempest and tend to lead their bearer somewhere new.

title: The Zones of the Labyrinth
summary: Frozen places within the realm of Oblivion.

claims.text: The Zones are fixed points in the Labyrinth untouched by time and Oblivion, prized for navigation; inside them the laws of the Underworld break down entirely.
Even the Spectre Hive-Mind fears the Zones, so an uneasy truce, like Cold War Berlin, holds there between wraiths and Spectres, though both sides break it quietly.
Renegades and thieves still slip past the blockades to raid them; older wraiths call these raiders jackals.

title: The Flayed Lands
summary: The dead realms of the Americas.

claims.text: The dead kingdoms of the Americas, the lands of Obsidian, Flint and Gold, were burned to ash in a frenzy of greed, and their fall is told as the clearest tale of Oblivion's fury.
In Mesoamerican memory the Olmecah first brought writing, art and faith; the wraith Mixcoatl, a king in life who stayed a king in death, was the first of the Mesoamerican dead.

title: The Bhuvar
summary: The Indian lands of the dead.

claims.text: Disasters in the living world of India, such as the 2004 tsunami and the yearly monsoon floods, echo as dangers in the Bhuvar, the realm of the dead beside it.
Some suspect Adharma drives such disasters to reap fresh dead and keep them off the wheel of rebirth.
Rural dead face vast plasmic beasts called the Children of Kali, and the monsoon there is known as the Feeding Time.
